_note: How an answer in Italian is compared (see sl.json for the fields). same: l' acqua is l'acqua (an apostrophe after a consonant is an elision; after a vowel it stands for an accent: perche'). fold: the accents (è for e, perchè or perche' for perché) are almost right, hint accent. loose: the apostrophe and the elided article (un amica for un'amica, la acqua or l acqua for l'acqua), ci and ne not elided before e (ci è for c'è, ci era for c'era, ce ne è for ce n'è) are almost right, hint apostrophe; lo or la before a form of avere only where the participle after it agrees (la ho vista for l'ho vista, lo ho visto for l'ho visto: almost; lo ho vista, la ho visto: the pronoun's gender wrong, wrong). wrong: the regular stem where a form has its own (anderò, averò, vederò, poterò for andrò, avrò, vedrò, potrò; ferò, sterò, derò for farò, starò, darò; mangierò, comincierò for mangerò, comincerò; the conditional's alike: anderei; venito, bevito, piacito for venuto, bevuto, piaciuto; B1's combined pronouns: the e of glie- left out, glilo, portaglilo, and the i kept before lo, la, ne on the end of a verb, dammilo, portamilo, darmilo for dammelo, portamelo, darmelo, each only for a glie- or -melo, -telo, -celo, -velo form (cavilo for cavolo, gagline for galline stay slips), as mi lo, ti la are wrong by their ending; the gerund with the other verbs' ending, leggando, dormando, bevando for leggendo, dormendo, bevendo, parlendo for parlando, and farendo, direndo, berendo for facendo, dicendo, bevendo; dicendoli, dandoli for dicendogli, dandogli, li for gli on a gerund; an article melted into di, da, in, a or su for another, B1's passive: della, alla or nella for dalla, delle for dalle, degli for dagli, only for another of them: della for bella stays a slip; B1's tenses and moods one letter off another's: the future's sarai, avrai, farai, darai for the conditional's sarei, avrei, farei, darei and the other way, the indicative's siamo and sta for the subjunctive's siano and stia, the remote past's fosti for the subjunctive's fossi and the other way, andò for the future's andrò, siete for siate; siano for siamo is left a slip, m and n side by side, for whoever hasn't met the subjunctive), matched against a word folded (no accents): wrong, never a slip in the stem. B1 too: glielo or gliela before avere is gliel', not elided almost only where the participle agrees, as lo and la (glielo ho dato, gliela ho data: almost; glielo ho data: wrong). ending_swaps: an ending typed for another on the same stem, where the subjunctive and the indicative differ a letter before the last two (dormono for dormano, dormano for dormono, parlano for parlino, parlate for parliate) and the conditional and the future (sarete for sareste): wrong, hint ending, never a slip in the stem; a slip elsewhere in such a word stays one (bambeno, bambimo for bambino; bambano is a swap). B2's forms: in wrong, paired, the imperfect subjunctive with another conjugation's vowel (dormessi for dormissi, dicassi for dicessi, dassi for dessi, parleste for parlaste), on a stem of three letters or more or av, st, d, so that a child's sassi, feste, classe, triste keep a slip as a slip, and -issimo as the right word left out, so bellessimo is one too; in ending_swaps, on the same stem, the passato remoto and the imperfetto or the future for one another (mangiavano for mangiarono, dormiranno for dormirono, parlavamo for parlammo); in wrong, paired, avando and essando for avendo and essendo, vede and vide for one another, mese for mise, foste and fosse, deste and desse, desti and dessi for one another (one letter inside the short stem).
